about: The map of the assessment engine: the twelve steps agreed with the school (docs/sources/assessment-workflow-v1.md) grouped as the four workflows (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1), every file that does each step, and the only connections one workflow may make to another. `packages/engine/tests/test_layout.py` fails the day the code and this map disagree; the website's How it works page draws it with live numbers. Edit this file when a step, a file or a connection changes — never the other way round.

workflows.name: Build the bank
workflows.does: Turns the school's skill sets into checked questions at four levels, ready for any paper.

workflows.name: Assemble and print
workflows.does: Chooses each child's next paper from their graph and prints the pack a teacher carries.

workflows.name: Read and graph
workflows.does: Reads what each child wrote, has a person check what the reader doubts, learns from every check, and puts the answers on the child's skill graph.

workflows.name: Close the loop
workflows.does: Turns the graph into Friday's class card, the home sheet and parent note, and the monthly report — and the next week's paper.

steps.name: Skill sets and the ladder
steps.does: Each skill written as what a child can do, with four levels and the cases each level holds; a person approves them once.

subject.note: The shape (skill → four levels → cases, approved once) is any subject's. The content is maths: the add/sub ladder, the 269 cases and the named mistakes are rows a new subject writes for itself — no code.

steps.name: Question bank
steps.does: Code makes every question from its level's rule and checks its answer; a model writes only story sentences; a person can correct or retire any question.
steps.who: code; a model for sentences; a person corrects

subject.note: Maths only: questions are generated and their answers computed by arithmetic code (engine/assess). A subject whose answers cannot be computed needs a person-approved key per question, which this step does not have.

steps.name: Old papers read in
steps.does: The papers children sat before the QR sheets are read into the same answers and evidence, so every child starts with a graph.

subject.note: Maths only: each old paper's answer key is maths, and the reader reads numbers. Marking moved to marking.py (N9).

steps.name: The week's declaration
steps.does: The teacher says what was taught this week, and the engine proposes the week's skill sets for her to confirm.
steps.who: a model structures, the teacher confirms

subject.note: Not built. Today a person names the week's skill set on the command line.

steps.name: Each child's next paper
steps.does: Makes each child's own paper from one request — skills, a level each, how many questions. A home paper's request comes from the child's graph: one skill, the weakest, at the level set by how often they were right, or a stretch one level up when they lag nowhere. A custom paper's comes from a teacher. Questions are random bank questions they have not seen, the ones that can show their repeated mistake first; a request the bank cannot fill is refused. The class's weekly paper still takes its skill set from the teacher. A teacher approves each paper, in their name, before it prints.

subject.note: Any subject: the rule reads states and levels, not maths.

steps.name: Worksheets and packs
steps.does: Every question sits on a numbered worksheet; each child gets one they have not sat, printed with a QR code, in handout order with spares.

subject.note: The library and packing are any subject's; how each kind of question is drawn on paper (engine/assess/render.py) is maths.

steps.name: Teacher approves the pack
steps.does: The teacher looks over the pack and its key and approves it before it is printed.

subject.note: Any subject. The WhatsApp tap to approve (n8n) is not built; approval is on the website.

steps.name: Capture
steps.does: A photographed or scanned paper is drawn as page images and lined up with the page it was printed from.

subject.note: Any subject. Scans enter from this Mac; a phone photo arriving on its own (Drive folder, QR) is not built.

steps.name: Read, check and learn
steps.does: The reader reads each answer with the child's notebook open, marks it by looking up the key, and sends what it doubts to a person; every check teaches it that child's handwriting.
steps.who: code reads and marks; a model proposes guesses; a person checks

subject.note: The loop — notebook, trust per kind, a person's check — is any subject's. The reader reads numbers only, and marking is a lookup against computed answers: a subject answered in words would reach a person every time.

steps.name: Evidence and the skill graph
steps.does: A signed-off answer becomes evidence for every skill it used, and each child's graph is rebuilt in six states.

subject.note: Any subject: evidence and the six states read skill codes, not maths. The rule runs in the database (confirm_results, rebuild_child_skill_state).

steps.name: Class card and home sheet
steps.does: Friday's class card, and a home sheet with a parent note for each child, aimed at what they got wrong.
steps.who: code; a model for one sentence; the teacher confirms

steps.name: Reports and planning
steps.does: Monthly parent reports, the class trend, regrouping and not-ready flags.
steps.who: code; a model for the narrative; the coordinator approves

shared.name: The maths library
shared.does: Pure code with no database: makes, measures, draws and marks every kind of question. W1, W2 and W3 all use it.

subject.note: All maths. A new subject brings its own library beside this one.

shared.name: The base
shared.does: The one database connection, the seed loader, and the class list every workflow reads.

shared.name: Outside services
shared.does: The only two files that talk to a service outside: the text model, and Amazon's handwriting reader.

shared.name: The proofs
shared.does: Every invariant over every row, a goal's commands and scenarios, the live site's health.

shared.name: The front doors
shared.does: The command line and the web service the website and n8n call — thin, each command handing straight to a workflow.

handovers.why: A worksheet is dealt from the bank's active questions, each read back as the question it is.
A child's paper is built from the bank's questions, each read back as the question it is.
A paper chosen from a child's graph is drawn from the bank's active questions, each read back as the question it is.
A question a person corrects or retires rebuilds the worksheets that held it.
A scanned library worksheet is counted off in copies as long as the worksheet prints.
A library worksheet copy is read against the page the worksheet prints: its questions' words, their pages, the name band.
